reported_value: Who Does the Communicative Work? Learners' Accounts of Supported Chinese-Language Encounters

Qualitative interview study using abductive within-case and across-case analysis of reported communicative encounters and recurrent practices; evaluations and hypothetical statements are distinguished.
One-year Chinese-language programme for foreign government officials in China
99 learners from 11 countries
Voluntary response to an open campus-network notice after ethical approval and project registration
All 59 completed and consented interviews met the inclusion criteria and formed the analytic corpus
A verified sample-wide age range is not available in the retained de-identified case-level records.
Beginner-oriented provision in aggregate project records; prior exposure varied and uniform individual baseline scores are unavailable.
Gender, education, individual baseline scores, and occupational-sector distributions were not uniformly retained and are not reconstructed
Government and public-service roles across multiple agencies
All interviews were completed during the approved implementation period; a uniform case-linked interview-date series is not retained in the de-identified analytic materials.
Four interviews online and 55 face to face
Approximately 7–128 minutes; median approximately 30 minutes
Experienced Chinese-language educators familiar with the programme, following a semi-structured guide and prompts for elaboration
Participants could use preferred home-country languages

Project documentation dates multilingual working-record preparation to January 2026 and describes language-familiar assistance and checks of machine- or AI-assisted drafts. Selected text can be checked against English working records; a complete excerpt-level audit against original-language recordings is not documented.
RMB 50 or an equivalent commemorative gift
The manuscript reports ethics approval and informed consent. Identifying approval details are supplied separately in the author-facing submission materials.
Bounded account of a communicative activity: particular encounter or recurrent practice, with evaluations and hypothetical statements retained separately.

Attribute message choice, wording source, delivery or presentation, and trouble-addressing action only when supported. Keep activity requirement, reported occurrence, outcome, and applicability separate. Shared means contributions to the same function; unestablished is not absence.
Retained de-identified archival numerical identifiers; leading zeros should be preserved
Recordings and complete transcripts remain restricted. This package supplies de-identified article-level materials and selected English working-record excerpts.
Reported action, participant interpretation and cross-case contrasts; not prevalence, turn-by-turn reconstruction or causal language-development effects.
The full 59-interview corpus is the analytic base; selected case summaries and source-location windows support traceability of central contrasts.
06_selected_source_windows.csv contains 19 windows from 10 included cases; 07_selected_evidence_excerpts.csv supplies selected text within those windows. Neither is an episode census.
